instruction.name: xvld
instruction.description: Read whole vector from memory address `addr + offset`, save the data into `dst`. Address misalignment does not raise an exception. Note that you can use this intrinsic to load floating point vectors, even though the return type represents integer vectors.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: xvld $xr0, $r20, 0; xvld $xr1, $r20, 32; xvld $xr2, $r20, 64; xvld $xr3, $r20, 96; xvld $xr4, $r20, 128; xvld $xr5, $r20, 160; xvld $xr6, $r20, 192; xvld $xr7, $r20, 224
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024' --asm 'xvld $xr0, $r20, 0; xvld $xr1, $r20, 32; xvld $xr2, $r20, 64; xvld $xr3, $r20, 96; xvld $xr4, $r20, 128; xvld $xr5, $r20, 160; xvld $xr6, $r20, 192; xvld $xr7, $r20, 224'

notes: Vector memory operation. Throughput measured with a hot 1KB stack buffer; latency not measured because it depends on cache/coherence state and needs a separate dependency chain.
